title: Customer registration, sign-in and account protection

sourcesRead.contributes: user story, identity API endpoints and auth, web shop sign-in entry point, seven Gherkin scenarios

context: As a customer I want to register and sign in, and I want my account protected against password guessing.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: Registration creates the customer without echoing the password Given a new customer with a unique e-mail address When their details are posted to POST /users/register Then the API responds 201 with the customer's details and an id And the response does not contain the password
acceptanceCriteria.text: Registration creates the customer without echoing the password: given a new customer with a unique e-mail address, when their details are posted to POST /users/register, then the API responds 201 with the customer's details and an id, and the response does not contain the password.
outcomes: the response contains the customer's details
the response does not contain the password

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: A registered e-mail address cannot register twice Given a customer already registered with an e-mail address When the same e-mail address is registered again Then the API responds 409 with the message "A customer with this email address already exists."
acceptanceCriteria.text: A registered e-mail address cannot register twice: given a customer already registered with an e-mail address, when the same e-mail address is registered again, then the API responds 409 with the message "A customer with this email address already exists."
outcomes: message "A customer with this email address already exists."

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: Weak passwords are rejected with every broken rule listed Given a new customer whose password is "abc" When they register Then the API responds 422 and the password errors state all four rules: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number
acceptanceCriteria.text: Weak passwords are rejected with every broken rule listed: given a new customer whose password is "abc", when they register, then the API responds 422 and the password errors state all four rules: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number.
outcomes: the password errors state the rule: at least 8 characters
the password errors state the rule: upper and lower case letters
the password errors state the rule: a symbol
the password errors state the rule: a number

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: Signing in on the web shop Given a registered customer on the web shop's sign-in page When they sign in with their e-mail address and password Then they land on the "My account" page And the navigation shows their first and last name
acceptanceCriteria.text: Signing in on the web shop: given a registered customer on the web shop's sign-in page, when they sign in with their e-mail address and password, then they land on the "My account" page and the navigation shows their first and last name.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop sign-in page ("Sign in" in the navigation)
outcomes: after signing in, the customer is on the "My account" page
the navigation shows the customer's first and last name

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: A wrong password is refused Given a registered customer When they sign in with a wrong password Then POST /users/login responds 401 And the web shop shows "Invalid email or password"
acceptanceCriteria.text: A wrong password is refused: given a registered customer, when they sign in with a wrong password, then POST /users/login responds 401 and the web shop shows "Invalid email or password".
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop sign-in page ("Sign in" in the navigation)
outcomes: POST /users/login with a wrong password responds 401
the web shop shows "Invalid email or password"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: The account locks after five failed attempts Given a registered customer When five sign-in attempts with a wrong password are made Then attempts one to five respond 401 And the sixth attempt, even with the correct password, responds 423 with a message that the account is locked
acceptanceCriteria.text: The account locks after five failed attempts: given a registered customer, when five sign-in attempts with a wrong password are made, then attempts one to five respond 401, and the sixth attempt, even with the correct password, responds 423 with a message that the account is locked.
outcomes: sign-in attempts one to five with a wrong password each respond 401
the sixth attempt, with the correct password, responds 423
the 423 response carries a message saying the account is locked

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: Signing out invalidates the token Given a signed-in customer with an access token When they sign out with GET /users/logout Then GET /users/me with the same token responds 401
acceptanceCriteria.text: Signing out invalidates the token: given a signed-in customer with an access token, when they sign out with GET /users/logout, then GET /users/me with the same token responds 401.
outcomes: GET /users/logout responds any 2xx success (body not checked) (G4, provided by the user)
after GET /users/logout, GET /users/me with the same token responds 401

endpoints.success: 201 with the customer's details and an id, without the password (story.md#L26-L27)
endpoints.request: the new customer's details (fields not stated)

rules.text: Password rules: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number
An e-mail address can be registered only once
The account locks after five failed sign-in attempts; while locked, sign-in responds 423 even with the correct password

errorModel.case: registering an e-mail address that is already registered
errorModel.body: A customer with this email address already exists.

errorModel.case: registering with a weak password ("abc"): the password errors state all four rules
signing in with a wrong password (attempts one to five); the web shop shows "Invalid email or password"
signing in to a locked account (the sixth attempt, even with the correct password), with a message that the account is locked
GET /users/me with a token that was signed out

auth.mechanism: Bearer token: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>, the access_token returned by POST /users/login

testData.strategy: not stated in the sources; AC-1 and AC-3 post a new customer with a unique e-mail address, AC-2 needs a customer already registered with an e-mail address, AC-6 needs a registered customer whose account the test locks

gaps.element: web shop sign-in page: its route (reached through "Sign in" in the navigation), how the e-mail, password and submit elements are found, and where the "Invalid email or password" message appears

tried.result: L19 says only that the sign-in page is reached through "Sign in" in the navigation; no route or element names

Route /auth/login (the navigation's "Sign in" link, href /auth/login). Fields by test id: getByTestId('email'), getByTestId('password'), submit getByTestId('login-submit') (label 'Password *' so getByLabel('Password', {exact:true}) matches nothing). A wrong password shows 'Invalid email or password' in getByTestId('login-error') under the form; the page stays on /auth/login

gaps.element: "My account" page and navigation: how the page is recognised, where the navigation shows the customer's name, and where the signed-in customer's first and last name come from (the seeded account's details)

tried.result: L42-L43 name the page and the navigation but give no route, locators or name source

After sign-in the app goes to /account; the page is recognised by heading 'My account' (h1, test id page-title, getByRole('heading', { name: 'My account' }) unique). The single navigation landmark (getByRole('navigation')) shows the signed-in customer's 'first_name last_name' as the nav-menu button; the name is the one the customer registered with (POST /users/register first_name/last_name, echoed by GET /users/me)
